'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023-present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Gaza war]]
***At least 50 [[Palestinians]] are killed in [[Israel]]i attacks across the [[Gaza Strip]], including 40 killed in [[Gaza City]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2025/9/18/live-israeli-army-applying-extreme-pressure-as-gaza-toll-passes-65000 (Al Jazeera)]
***A [[Jordan]]ian truck driver bringing aid to the [[Gaza Strip]] kills two [[Israel]]i military personnel before being fatally shot by security personnel at the [[Allenby Bridge]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israeli-military-says-received-report-shooting-jordan-border-crossing-2025-09-18/ (Reuters)]
***The [[United States and the United Nations|United States]] casts its sixth [[United Nations Security Council veto power|veto]] over a draft [[United Nations Security Council]] [[United Nations resolution|resolution]] calling for a permanent [[ceasefire]] in Gaza, the lifting of [[Israeli blockade of aid delivery to the Gaza Strip|Israeli restrictions on aid]], and the release of all [[Gaza war hostage crisis|hostages]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-vetoes-un-demand-ceasefire-aid-access-gaza-2025-09-18/ (Reuters)]
**[[Red Sea crisis]]
***A [[Houthi]] drone attack damages a hotel in [[Eilat]], [[Israel]]. [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/article-867996 (''Jerusalem Post'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/drone-launched-yemen-crashes-israels-eilat-2025-09-18/ (Reuters)]
*[[Insurgency in Balochistan]]
**Two security personnel are killed and twenty-three others are injured when a [[Suicide attack|suicide]] [[car bomb]] targets a security convoy in [[Turbat]], [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]], [[Pakistan]]. Meanwhile, six people are killed in a separate car bombing in [[Chaman]]. [https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-car-bombings-southwest-balochistan-52123957204e94674f16ebf7539432d0 (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*At least ten people are killed and 25 others are injured when a fire breaks out in a high-rise office building in [[Lagos]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cr704re0kmpo (BBC News)]
*Three people, including musician [[Brett James]], are killed when James's [[Cirrus SR22T]] aircraft crashes near [[Macon County Airport]] in [[North Carolina]], [[United States]]. '''International relations'''
*[[Poland–Ukraine relations]], [[2025 Russian drone incursion into Poland]]
**[[Ukraine]] announces it will train [[Poland|Polish]] [[Polish Armed Forces|troops]] and engineers in [[Drone warfare|counter-drone]] operations following recent [[Russia]]n drone incursions into Polish [[airspace]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/9/18/ukraine-pledges-to-bolster-polish-drone-defence-with-training (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Syria–United States relations]]
**[[Syria]]n [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates (Syria)|foreign minister]] [[Asaad al-Shaibani]] visits [[Washington, D.C.]] to attend meetings with the [[World Bank]] and the [[International Monetary Fund]], and to meet with [[Israel]]i delegations and [[U.S. secretary of state]] [[Marco Rubio]], marking the first time a [[Syrian transitional government|Syrian official]] has visited the [[United States]] in 25 years. [https://apnews.com/article/syria-us-asaad-alshibani-trump-sanctions-alsharaa-526af7ef1ad6afc5ad1086e0707a5720 (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Egypt]]'s [[Ministry of Interior (Egypt)|interior ministry]] reports that a 3,000-year-old gold bracelet belonging to the [[pharaoh]] [[Amenemope (pharaoh)|Amenemope]], missing from the [[Egyptian Museum]] in [[Cairo]], was stolen, [[Gold laundering|melted]] and sold, with several suspects arrested. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c1kw8dwy4dro (BBC News)]
*[[Iraq]] receives 47 [[French people|French]] nationals previously detained in northeast Syria on suspicion of [[Islamic State]] membership for prosecution on [[Islamic terrorism|terrorism]] charges. '''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025 Albanian parliamentary election]]
**[[Albania]]n [[Prime Minister of Albania|prime minister]] [[Edi Rama]] begins an unprecedented [[Rama IV Government|fourth term]] following the [[Socialist Party of Albania|Socialist Party]]'s victory in the last election. [https://www.reuters.com/world/albanias-rama-starts-fourth-term-pm-targets-eu-membership-2025-09-18/ (Reuters)]
*[[Censorship in the Maldives]]
**[[Maldives|Maldivian]] [[President of the Maldives|president]] [[Mohamed Muizzu]] ratifies the [[Maldives Media and Broadcasting Regulation Law|Media and Broadcasting Regulation Law]], which allows fines, license suspensions, and closures of media outlets found in violation of its provisions. [https://apnews.com/article/maldives-media-freedom-law-muizzi-license-journalist-2ca60d731492ef11840850d76f7007e1 (AP)]
*[[Bulgaria]]n [[Prime Minister of Bulgaria|prime minister]] [[Rosen Zhelyazkov]]'s [[Zhelyazkov Government|government]] survives their fifth [[vote of no-confidence]] this year over alleged failures to reform the justice and [[National security of Bulgaria|security sectors]], with 133 [[National Assembly (Bulgaria)|lawmakers]] opposing and 101 supporting the motion. [https://www.reuters.com/world/bulgarias-government-survives-fifth-no-confidence-vote-2025-09-18/ (Reuters)]
